subject.title: fix(telegram): long-running sends leak connections after cache evictions

question: Is the focused lease coverage plus local Bot API live-output proof enough to land this Telegram transport lifetime change, or should it first get a real Telegram transport probe?
rationale: The patch looks correct from source review, focused regressions, and dependency checks, but transport lifetime mistakes can interrupt outbound Telegram delivery in ways green unit tests may not fully settle.

options.title: Accept Focused Proof
options.body: Proceed with maintainer review and merge once exact-head checks stay green, accepting the remaining delivery-lifecycle risk as covered by the focused regressions and local live-output proof.

options.title: Require Live Telegram Probe
options.body: Ask for a real Telegram or Crabbox transport probe that demonstrates eviction does not interrupt an outbound operation before merge.

options.title: Pause For Redesign
options.body: Hold the PR only if the Telegram owner wants a broader API-client lifetime refactor instead of the current send-cache lease design.

recommendation.title: Accept Focused Proof
recommendation.body: Proceed with maintainer review and merge once exact-head checks stay green, accepting the remaining delivery-lifecycle risk as covered by the focused regressions and local live-output proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the documented Telegram subsystem owner and have directly related transport fallback history.
